period_note: Year-end position from the Annual Report's own multi-year 'Five-Year Business Summary' table (audited), Solo basis. Reporting basis (Solo vs Consolidated) confirmed by matching this dataset's recorded total assets against the annual report's own balance sheets: the standalone 'BALANCE SHEET' reports Total Property and Assets of BDT 444,690,299,923 (=444,690.30m, matches this record and the Five-Year table exactly), while 'MERCANTILE BANK PLC. AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES / CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEET' reports BDT 447,583,942,554 (=447,583.94m) for the same date -- Solo is the basis used throughout this dataset (consistent with FY2011-2023). Total liabilities not directly given as a line in the Five-Year table; calculated as total assets minus shareholders' equity (matches the raw Balance Sheet's own reported Total Liabilities of 418,880,240,077 almost exactly). MAJOR FINDING: FY2024 discloses a large loan-loss provisioning shortfall. Per Note 7.8 ('Required provision for Loans and advances/investments'), required provision against loans/advances was BDT 38,167.71m against BDT 21,159.11m maintained -- a shortfall of BDT 17,008.60m (44.6% underprovisioned vs requirement). Per the note: Bangladesh Bank's letter Ref. DBI-4/110/2025-655 (dated 29 April 2025) initially assessed a shortfall of BDT 2,121.19 crore (=21,211.9m) against BDT 220.33 crore then held, i.e. an initial shortfall of BDT 1,900.86 crore (=19,008.6m); a subsequent Bangladesh Bank directive (reference contains Bangla-script text that did not extract cleanly from the source PDF; dated 22 May 2025) permitted the Bank to transfer BDT 200.00 crore from FY2024 pre-provision profit into specific provisions, reducing the final disclosed shortfall to BDT 1,700.86 crore (=17,008.60m, the figure reconciled in the table above). Bangladesh Bank granted regulatory forbearance to finalize FY2024 financials without full provisioning adjustment; consequently no dividend was declared for FY2024 (0% across cash/stock). This provisioning shortfall was disclosed only via a note-level asterisk in the FY2024 financial statements -- the independent auditors' report for FY2024 does NOT contain a formal 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph on this (unlike FY2025, where it does -- see 2025_Q4.json). required_capital is a directly REPORTED figure this year (Note 14.5/14.6, 'Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR)' = Total RWA x 12.5% including the 2.5% capital conservation buffer), not calculated -- it reconciles exactly against Total Capital minus the reported Capital Surplus (38,748.56 - 1,683.77 = 37,064.79). CROSS-VALIDATED against the FY2025 annual report's comparative column for FY2024, which reproduces every figure below identically. DISCREPANCY NOTE (does not affect any stored year): both the FY2024 and FY2025 reports' own Five-Year tables show FY2023 Paid-up Capital as 11,065.23m in their comparative column, but the FY2023 report's own audited balance sheet -- and this dataset's already-stored 2023_Q4.json -- record 11,065.75m, which also matches the unchanged Dec-23 raw balance-sheet comparative (11,065,754,350) printed in both the FY2024 and FY2025 reports' own audited 'BALANCE SHEET' statements. This appears to be a typo in the bank's own Five-Year summary table row, repeated across two report vintages; the FY2023 record is left unchanged per this dataset's restatement policy.
